newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-HENRY CONSIDERS ENGLAND COACHING OFFER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HENRY CONSIDERS ENGLAND COACHING OFFER.

text.p: New Zealander Graham Henry, coach of Super 12 rugby union champions Auckland, said on Monday he wanted to coach England after confirming Twickenham officials had spoken to him about a job.
But Henry said any contract with the Rugby Football Union (RFU) would have to include a clause guaranteeing him an opportunity to coach the England senior side at some point.
"I've been discussing things with England and an opportunity to coach there...and hopefully their contract will involve the English 15," Henry told Auckland's 1ZB radio station.
Jack Rowell has guided England's fortunes for the past three years but his current contract expires next month. The coach also has various business commitments.
Asked directly about his prospects of coaching England, Henry suggested he might have to wait for his chance. "Maybe in time. But that's about all I can say," he said.
The RFU, reacting to media reports suggesting Henry had been approached to lead England's 1999 World Cup campaign, issued a statement last week saying no formal talks had taken place.

The RFU said no decision on Rowell's future would be taken until England had returned home from Australia, where the Wallabies won a one-off test 25-6 on Saturday in what could prove to be his last match in charge.

Henry said coaching the England senior side after a set period of time would be one of his conditions. "We've had discussions and it's just a matter of looking at the contract I guess and making a decision," he said.
Henry said he had been in talks for nearly three months but nothing was on paper as yet. A decision was likely to be made before the end of July, he said.
Asked by Reuters to comment further, Henry said the media reports were not accurate.

"It's not true. I've talked to people from England but that's as far as it goes at this stage. All I've done is had discussions with England as everybody knows, about a coaching opportunity," he said.
The English moves have alarmed New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU) officials.
Chief executive David Moffett and chairman Rob Fisher are in Britain this week talking to the home unions, and among the topics is player and coach poaching.
However, New Zealand, has little to offer Henry.

Incumbent coach John Hart is almost certain to take New Zealand to the World Cup and, according to media reports, Hart would not welcome Henry into his coaching team because they have a different philosophy to the game.
